newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends off on book-squaring, Saudi comment.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends off on book-squaring, Saudi comment.

text.p: IPE Brent crude closed weaker on Friday, depressed by thin pre-holiday long liquidation and remarks by a senior Saudi Arabian official that the Kingdom would not automatically cut output if the U.N. lifted santions on Iraq, dealers said.
"That certainly encouraged a test of support at $23.60 (a barrel on Feb Brent) but the market was pretty rangebound in Europe," said a broker.
Feb Brent closed down 52 cents at the session's low of $23.46 a barrel. It touched a high of $23.94 early in the session after opening at $23.73.

Deputy oil minister Prince Abdul Aziz bin Salman, speaking during an interview on Middle East Broadcasting Corp., said Saudi Arabia would not necessarily trim its output to make room for Iraq, which has recently begun limited exports for the first time since the Gulf War under a U.N. oil-for-food deal.
Brokers said the reports prompted knee-jerk selling by local floor traders but prices soon found support against a background of tight supply and strong winter demand in the U.S.
The main factor behind Friday's modest retracement -- Brent is still only $1.50 a barrel off its post-Gulf War high posted in October -- was pre-holiday book squaring, dealers said.
Earlier, IPE gas oil closed lower as the front month backwardation came under heavy pressure from a lack of prompt demand on physical spot markets in northwest Europe, traders said.
Jan gas oil closed $2.75 lower at $215.00 a tonne as the Jan/Feb intermonth spread shed $2.00 to close at just +$1.50.
"We're due for a lot of cold weather in the States, but (the effects) just haven't kicked in over here yet," a broker said.
